tEn: Design Engineering in the AI Era: A Conversation with Flora Guo
tZh: AI 时代的设计工程：与 Flora Guo 的对话
sEn: Flora Guo discusses how AI can supercharge design processes and shares insights from her career at Vercel and Paradigm.
sZh: Flora Guo 探讨 AI 如何赋能设计流程，并分享她在 Vercel 和 Paradigm 的职业见解。

consensus.en: AI gives us a map of the territory, but we must still walk the terrain and build our own understanding.
consensus.zh: AI 能给我们一张地形图，但亲自行走、建立自己的理解仍要靠我们自己。

consensus.en: Luck has a geometry and can be cultivated by increasing surface area, awareness, and opportunities for serendipity.
consensus.zh: 运气有几何结构，可以通过扩大表面积、提升觉察和创造机缘来经营。

consensus.en: Sharing your work and being a generous host online creates unexpected career opportunities and community.
consensus.zh: 在线上分享作品并做慷慨的东道主，会带来意想不到的职场机会与社群连接。

consensus.en: Design engineering means translating intention into real user experience, not just making pretty artifacts.
consensus.zh: 设计工程意味着把意图转化为真实的用户体验，而不只是做出好看的产物。

consensus.en: Use AI as an infinitely patient tutor to scaffold learning, build context, and deepen mental models.
consensus.zh: 把 AI 当作无限耐心的导师，用脚手架式学习构建上下文和更深的心智模型。

consensus.en: Learn by building: acquire minimum viable knowledge, then backfill understanding through projects.
consensus.zh: 在构建中学习：先掌握最小可行知识，再通过项目回填理解。

contrarian.en: Rather than extracting from people, ask what you can offer; hosting spaces creates more luck than self-promotion.
contrarian.zh: 与其向别人索取，不如问自己能给予什么；主办空间比自我推销更能带来好运。

contrarian.en: AI outputs are not grounded in understanding; when you need to debug, you still need foundational knowledge.
contrarian.zh: AI 生成的产物并不等于真正理解；一旦需要调试，你仍需扎实的基础知识。

contrarian.en: Do not choose a design direction too early; align on conceptual primitives before visual exploration.
contrarian.zh: 不要过早选择设计方案；先对齐概念原语，再开始视觉探索。

contrarian.en: Designers at AI-native startups can be non-traditional: own front-end and code, not just visual design.
contrarian.zh: 在 AI 原生创业公司，设计师可以不走传统路径：不只做视觉，还要拥有前端和代码。

contrarian.en: Even with AI, going back to basics and studying how components work is increasingly valuable.
contrarian.zh: 即使有 AI，回归基础、研究组件如何运作也变得越来越有价值。

transcript.sec: Sharing online and being a host

turns.en: This project in itself is almost an inception of that very idea, because you've shared this thing that you enjoyed and put it out on the internet. I don't remember how many impressions it got on Twitter, but it was a lot — it was almost like 100,000 or something. People obviously enjoyed your work; this resonated with them. And that makes me wonder how intentionally you are stewarding your own surface area for luck. Maybe you could talk a little bit about the role that sharing online has played in your own career journey.
turns.zh: 这个项目本身就是那个想法的开端——你把自己喜欢的东西分享出来，放到了互联网上。我不记得它在 Twitter 上获得了多少曝光，但非常多，差不多有 10 万。大家显然很欣赏你的作品，产生了共鸣。这让我好奇，你在多大程度上是有意经营自己的“运气表面积”的。你能不能聊一聊，在线分享在你自己的职业生涯里扮演了怎样的角色？

turns.en: There's this quote that I often return to by, I think, either Ray or Charles Eames, which is that the role of a designer is that of a very good host. And I think showing up in today's world — where, like you said, it is ultra-competitive and there is a lot of stuff going on all the time with all these new tools — really comes down to asking, what can we give? Whether it's holding space for an event or creating an artifact about something that we're excited about and want to share. Really flipping the script from 'what can I ask of this person?' to 'what can I offer them?' That's something I want to keep returning to in the ways we show up online or in person, especially when we host events. Inviting people into a space, thinking about, what can I gather them around? What is the intention I can set around this? The ways we host space online are very similar. Whether it's gathering people around a common interest — like we're going to screen a design film — or inviting them to show off their own work, it's really about figuring out what are the threads that connect all of us together. What is the reason for us to be together in this space? And then figuring out how can I pull this out of others as well. I'm incredibly grateful to the people I've gotten to meet online. People who start off — maybe you just like seeing each other's projects, you're like, 'Wow, this is really cool.' Then you send them a DM, and it kicks off maybe a conversation IRL over coffee or a phone call, and then it sparks either collaboration over projects or even roles. When I was working as an independent designer for a couple of years, I would say the vast majority of my clients came in from Twitter. As someone who's always loved experimenting, trying things out for the heck of it, it's been such a great way to meet people with similar interests. Even my current role felt very serendipitous — how Anna, my CEO, found me online on Twitter. And when I was at Bracel as well, it was just through conversations that started off in the DMs. So I think any designer who's building projects — it's just such an incredible time that we live in to get to share with the internet online.
turns.zh: 我经常想到一句出处可能是 Ray 或 Charles Eames 的话：设计师的角色，就是一位非常好的主人。我觉得在当今这个世界里——就像你说的，竞争极度激烈，新的工具层出不穷——真正的问题在于：我们能给予什么？无论是为一场活动腾出空间，还是为自己感到兴奋、想要分享的东西创作一件作品。把问题反过来：不是“我能从这个人身上得到什么”，而是“我能为他们提供什么”。这就是我想反复回到的思考方式，无论我们在线上还是线下出现，尤其是当我们主办活动的时候。邀请人们进入一个空间，想一想：我可以用什么把他们聚在一起？我能围绕这件事设定怎样的意图？我们在线上营造空间的方式也非常相似。无论是围绕一个共同兴趣把大家聚起来，比如一起看一部设计电影，还是邀请他们展示自己的作品，关键都是找到连接彼此的那条线索。我们为什么要在同一个空间里？然后也想一想，我该如何把别人身上的这些东西也激发出来。我对我遇到的每一个线上朋友都充满感激。有些人一开始只是觉得对方的项目很酷，于是你发了一条私信，慢慢变成线下的咖啡或电话，再之后可能激发出项目上的合作，甚至是工作机会。我自己做独立设计师那几年，绝大部分客户都来自 Twitter。作为一个一直喜欢折腾、喜欢为了好玩而尝试新事物的人，这真是认识志同道合者的绝佳方式。甚至连我现在这份工作，也充满了机缘巧合——我的 CEO Anna 是在 Twitter 上发现我的。还有我在 Bracel 的时候，一切也都是从私信里的对话开始的。所以我觉得，任何正在做项目的设计师，我们生活的时代真的太棒了，可以把自己的作品分享到网上。

turns.en: Can you go a little bit deeper into how intentionally you are nurturing the community you've built for yourself on Twitter? I think a lot of people look at where you're at, and it's really inspiring, but also a bit of a black box in terms of how to even get to that point where, all of a sudden, Twitter really is a very big deal for your career.
turns.zh: 你能不能更深地聊一聊，你是在多大程度上有意经营自己在 Twitter 上建立起来的社群？我觉得很多人看到你现在的状态，会觉得非常受鼓舞，但同时也像面对一个黑箱：到底是怎么一步步走到 Twitter 突然成为事业中很重要一部分的？

turns.en: I remember way back in March of 2022, that's when I first got onto Twitter. It was just me sharing things that I was really excited about — going to events IRL and being like, 'Oh wow, I just learned about X thing in design. Here are my takeaways.' Just showing up, being excited, and really down to have conversations, I think, led one thing to another. Different roles that started off from a DM would evolve into in-person things, like hosting an event together, or eventually working together. People can really feel the excitement you have, whether it's through a project or through notes or something that you're hosting. So it's just about creating things that are artifacts of what you love and what you're passionate about, and putting them online.
turns.zh: 我记得那是在 2022 年 3 月，我第一次上 Twitter。一开始只是分享我感到兴奋的东西——去线下活动，然后说“哇，我刚学到了设计里的某个东西，这是我的收获”。就是不断出现、保持热情、真的很愿意聊天，我想这让我一步一步走到了今天。很多从私信开始的机会，后来变成了线下的事情，比如一起办活动，或者最后一起共事。人们真的能感受到你的热情，无论通过一个项目、一些笔记，还是你主办的活动。所以就是去创造那些承载你所爱和所热情之事的作品，然后把它们放到网上。

turns.en: There's putting things out there on the internet and being a magnet for people who care. And then there's also proactively messaging others and being the one who initiates. How much are you doing the latter? I think that's something that's so valuable, and yet a little bit scary probably for a lot of people listening.
turns.zh: 一种是把东西放到网上，成为吸引同频之人的磁铁；另一种是主动给别人发消息，成为发起对话的那个人。你主动做的比例有多大？我觉得这是非常有价值的事，但对很多听众来说可能也有点可怕。

turns.en: Whenever there's a designer whose work you really admire, I love dropping a quick note and saying, 'Hey, I love what you shipped. Here in particular is what really resonated with me.' And whenever I get those in my inbox, it really makes my day. I would say hosting events is also a really great way to reach out to people and to have them reach out to you as well. Whether it's hosting a design film night, a design engineering PowerPoint night, or something about agentic interfaces, I think it's about creating very specific things that you can offer people. Like, 'Oh, come into my home or come into my office, I'd love to host you.' Or sending them something you think they'd enjoy. Just create moments where it feels so much more natural — you're just talking to a new friend on the internet.
turns.zh: 每当遇到作品让我特别欣赏的设计师，我就喜欢发一条简短的消息说：“嘿，我很喜欢你发布的东西，尤其是这里，真的让我很有共鸣。”所以每当我收到这样的私信，一整天都会很开心。我觉得主办活动也是非常好的方式，既能主动触达别人，也能让别人来触达你。无论是办一场设计电影之夜、设计工程 PowerPoint 之夜，还是跟智能体式界面相关的活动，关键在于创造一些非常具体、可以提供给别人的东西。比如“来我家吧，或者来我办公室，我很想招待你”，或者给他们寄一些你觉得他们会喜欢的东西。去创造一些让人感觉更自然的时刻——你只是在和网上一个新朋友聊天。

transcript.sec: The path to Vercel and v0

turns.en: I think the reason why I had so many follow-up questions on this category of topics is that I look at your journey and I see an incredibly steep trajectory — like how fast you've been able to really insert yourself and build momentum in this space. And now you're at Paradigm, working this high-profile role. It's really cool, right? A goal of mine in this conversation is to help people find little pieces of that equation that they can use to reverse engineer your trajectory. So maybe we could talk a little bit more about what that journey has looked like, starting with the design engineering internship at Vercel.
turns.zh: 我之所以在这类话题上一直追问，是因为我看你的经历，会看到一条非常陡峭的成长曲线——你能以多快的速度真正切入这个领域并建立起势头，现在又在 Paradigm 担任这个备受瞩目的角色，真的很酷，对吧？我这场对话的目标之一，就是帮大家找到这个方程式里的小碎片，让他们能逆向推导你的轨迹。所以，或许我们可以再多聊聊这段旅程，从你在 Vercel 的设计工程实习开始。

turns.en: Vercel is a company that I've looked up to for many, many years, even before I knew what a deployment was. I remember being on their homepage and thinking, 'Wow, this is just so beautifully built out.' I actually started this design engineering journey with V0. I remember back in 2024, I was looking around and seeing such incredible projects popping up in my timeline and having no idea where to start. I think the incredible thing about these tools is that you can go in with just an idea and start noodling out what the path looks like to creating something that I'm really proud of. So I started off with making shaders — things that looked like sunrise — and then moved on to personal projects in V0 as well. One I really had a lot of fun making was this idea of a digital gift box. I feel like that was the first project where I just sat down and was like, 'Okay, today I'm going to make something.' I really love the idea of software as a gift.
turns.zh: Vercel 是我仰望了很多很多年的公司，甚至在我还不知道什么是部署的时候。我记得自己看着它的首页，心想：“哇，这个网站做得真漂亮。”其实我是从 V0 开始这段设计工程之旅的。我记得 2024 年，我四处张望，看到时间线上冒出来那么多令人惊叹的项目，完全不知道从哪里开始。我觉得这些工具了不起的地方在于，你可以只带着一个想法进去，然后就慢慢摸索出通往一个让我自己自豪的作品的路径。所以我一开始做的是着色器——比如日出的效果——之后也在 V0 里做个人项目。其中一个我做得特别开心的，是“数字礼物盒”的想法。我觉得那是第一个我坐下来对自己说“好，今天我要做点东西”的项目。我真的很喜欢“软件即礼物”这个想法。

turns.en: And I think for everyone, it really depends on the context: whether you just want to create a fun demo or prototype, or whether this is a product that you want to sustain over time.
turns.zh: 我觉得对每个人来说，这真的取决于具体的语境：你是只想做一个好玩的演示或原型，还是想做一个需要长期维护的产品。

turns.en: Yeah, it goes back to what you were talking about in terms of viewing AI as the ultimate personalized tutor.
turns.zh: 嗯，这又回到了你之前说的，把 AI 视为终极的个性化导师。

turns.en: Yeah, exactly. And actively finding ways to lean into that, rather than just to accomplish your next goal and then your next goal.
turns.zh: 是的，完全如此。而且要主动去利用这一点，而不是仅仅完成一个又一个目标。

turns.en: Absolutely. It's like: how can we use AI to really supercharge our own process as learners, thinkers, and designers? I feel confident in saying that you have supercharged a lot of people's process listening, because the way that you think about these tools, but also the way that you approach your own journey and your hunger for learning and experimentation, it's super inspiring for us. So I really, really appreciate you coming on and sharing it with us today.
turns.zh: 确实如此。这就像是：我们该如何用 AI 真正加速我们作为学习者、思考者和设计师的成长过程？我可以很自信地说，你已经加速了许多正在收听的人的过程，因为你思考这些工具的方式，以及你对待自己旅程的方式，还有你对学习和实验的渴望，都让我们深受启发。所以，真的非常感激你今天能来和我们分享这些。

turns.en: Yeah, thank you so much, Red. It's been such a pleasure.
turns.zh: 嗯，非常感谢你，Red。这真的很愉快。

turns.en: Before I let you go, I want to take just 1 minute to run you through my favorite products because I'm constantly asked what's in my stack. Framer is how I build websites. Genway is how I do research. Granola is how I take notes during crit. Jitter is how I animate my designs. Lovable is how I build my ideas in code. Mobbin is how I find design inspiration. Paper is how I design like a creative. And Raycast is my shortcut every step of the way. Now, I've hand-selected these companies so that I can do these episodes full-time. So, by far, the number one way to support the show is to check them out. You can find the full list at dive.club/partners.
turns.zh: 在你走之前，我想用一分钟介绍一下我最喜欢的产品，因为经常有人问我用什么工具。Framer 是我建网站的工具。Genway 是我做研究用的。Granola 是评审时我做笔记用的。Jitter 是我做设计动画用的。Lovable 是我用代码实现想法用的。Mobbin 是我找设计灵感用的。Paper 是我像创意人一样做设计用的。Raycast 则是每步都离不开的快捷工具。这些公司都是我精心挑选的，这样我才能全职做这些节目。所以，目前支持这个节目最有效的方式就是去了解一下它们。你可以在 dive.club/partners 找到完整列表。
